hypothesis: At least one of the four technical categories (trend, momentum, volume, chart_pattern) carries information about forward returns on its own, even though the weighted combination (E001) does not.
acceptance_criterion: PRE-REGISTERED before running. A category 'carries information at horizon H' only if the Spearman rank correlation between its score and the H-hour forward return has a block-bootstrap 95% interval that excludes zero with the SAME sign in BOTH exploration and validation. Sign is reported as-is: a consistently NEGATIVE correlation means the category points the wrong way for that horizon (a finding, not a pass). Ablation and redundancy results are descriptive (no criterion) and feed the next experiment's design only.

target.definition: forward return (continuous) for correlation; three-class fixed 0.5% band for ablation balanced accuracy
target.outcome: close of candle opening at as_of+H

metrics.ablation: no leave-one-out variant produces a validation edge whose interval excludes zero; removing chart_pattern raises 3-class balanced accuracy to 0.36-0.38 only because HOLD rises to 50% and NEUTRAL is the majority label at short horizons
metrics.per_year_edge_24h: every category flips sign across years

results: NO CATEGORY CARRIES POSITIVE INFORMATION at any horizon. Two categories carry a small, consistent NEGATIVE relationship at the 1-hour horizon: momentum and volume scores are slightly anti-correlated with the next hour's return in both periods (|rho| 0.02-0.04) -- i.e. after an hour that looks strong on RSI/MACD or on above-average volume with a rising price, the next hour tends very slightly to give some back (short-term mean reversion). This explains E001's 'SELL hours went up' clue. The effect is real but far too weak to make a usable signal (a correlation of 0.03 explains about 0.1% of the variance). Trend and chart_pattern are 69% correlated (built from the same moving averages) and neither relates to future returns consistently. The exploration-period decile shape for trend (top deciles earn more at 24h) does not survive validation.
consistent_across_time: No positive relationship is consistent. The 1h negative relationship for momentum and volume IS consistent across both periods.
leakage_check: uses only the E001 replay (point-in-time by construction) and timestamp-based forward returns; a negative finding is not what leakage produces
overfitting_suspected: no -- nothing tuned. Note: 20 tests were run; two passed with a negative sign and consistent across periods, which is more than the ~1 expected by chance, but the effect size is tiny.
affected_design: Yes: (1) the existing technical categories are not a foundation to build on -- new information sources are needed, not re-weighting; (2) flipping momentum's sign is NOT done: it would be fitting to the data we just looked at, and at |rho|~0.03 it would not produce a usable signal anyway; recorded as a finding only; (3) chart_pattern is redundant with trend and could be dropped for simplicity when scoring is next revised -- not now (baseline stays frozen).
notes: Next per the brief: feature groups in order, starting with volatility and regime, each with a pre-registered criterion and the same bench. Also the AI-component tests (Part M) are still pending.
